look_here_first: CHECK THE TRUE NECTAR GLAND, NOT THE VARIABLE LEAVES. Euphorbia heterophylla (painted spurge) has usually GREEN or pale-green upper bracts, often highly variable leaf outlines, a smooth developing THREE-LOBED capsule, and ONE yellow-green cyathial nectar gland with a RAISED CIRCULAR/ANNULAR RIM. The exact saved SAplants var. heterophylla macro now SHOWS and annotates that ROUND rimmed gland opening. E. cyathophora normally has red/pink/white patches at bract bases, but some plants have all-green bracts; its gland is distinctly OBLONG and lacks the raised circular rim. The salmon-pink-bracted older Psumuseum photograph labeled E. heterophylla is on TAXON ID HOLD, so do not teach from or publish that image until identity is resolved. Nativity/range status unchanged.

key_traits.label: Family pattern
key_traits.text: Euphorbia: milky latex; the apparent flower is a cyathium with highly reduced male flowers and one central female flower.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Highly polymorphic within populations and even on one plant; blades may be lanceolate, elliptic, obovate, pandurate, or lobed. Leaf shape alone is unreliable.

key_traits.label: Upper bracts
key_traits.text: Pleiochasial bracts remain green or are only paler green at the base rather than sharply red/pink/white as is typical of E. cyathophora.

key_traits.label: Cyathium
key_traits.text: One yellow-green gland, stipitate and clavate, about 1–1.4 × 1–1.2 mm; opening circular, occasionally flattened by pressing, with a distinct annular rim; appendages absent.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 2.8–3.8 × 4–5.3 mm, three-lobed, usually glabrous and only rarely sparsely puberulent.

key_traits.label: Seed
key_traits.text: Seeds broadly deltoid, about 2.4–2.8 × 1.9–2.4 mm, angular in cross section with a strongly keeled dorsal face and tubercles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Annual upright herb; can resemble toothed spurges and wild poinsettia.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Upper bracts usually green or paler near base in FNA; colored-looking specimens need recheck.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Leaves extremely variable, from unlobed to deeply cut, often on one specimen.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Terminal green cyathial cups and glabrous three-lobed capsules.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Single clavate stalked nectar gland with round opening and annular rim is main distinction; macro missing.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Texas occurrence comparison-only per existing project, not automatically approved native.

key_traits.label: Reproductive teaching
key_traits.text: Cyathium = a cup-shaped Euphorbia inflorescence with highly reduced staminate flowers and one pistillate flower. The stalked swelling outside the cup becomes a THREE-LOBED capsule; upper colored or green modified leaves are BRACTS and not five separate petals. Do not mistake a ripe fruit for the nectar gland.

lookalikes.differences: Against E. cyathophora, use the cyathial gland before leaf shape. E. heterophylla = green/pale bracts + stipitate gland + round annular-rimmed opening; E. cyathophora = sharply colored bract bases + sessile/substipitate gland + oblong rimless opening.
